chunks: All praise is due to Allah, from Whose mercy no one loses hope, from Whose bounty no one is deprived, from Whose forgiveness no one is disappointed, and for Whose worship no one is too proud. His mercy never departs from Him, and His bounty is never lost.

key_terms.مَقْنُوطٍ: One who has lost hope or despair
key_terms.مُسْتَنْكَفٍ: Too proud or haughty to do something

ai.seo_question: What are the four aspects of Allah's attributes praised in this supplication from Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this opening invocation of *Du'a al-Faraj*, Imam Ali (AS) establishes a theological foundation of hope (*raja'*) and gratitude (*shukr*), countering despair (*qanoot*) with the certainty of divine mercy. This structure reflects the Shia emphasis on balancing awe with love, framing worship not as a duty of obligation but as a natural response to the inseparable nature of God's bounty and forgiveness.
